name: Possession pragmatism (controlled possession)
scopeNote: Possession used to control risk and the opponent's chances (the ball as a defensive tool, few shots faced, deliberate slowing), not possession as an end or as dominance by pressing. Two windows: Del Bosque's Spain (World Cup 2010, Euro 2012; start 2008-07-15 is the unverified date already in the Del Bosque manager file, end ~2012-07-01 Euro final) and Arteta's early Arsenal (appointed 2019-12-20 per TBS/FourFourTwo, window cut at the end of 2021-22, about 2022-05-22, approximate, not checked in a source). Sources that name it: Irish Times (Spain's game 'can be summed up in a word: control'; 'Tiki-taka always had a defensive facet'); Analytics FC and Opta Analyst for Arsenal ('calculated possession style'; 'rigid possession system straight out of the Guardiola playbook' then loosened). Distinct from tiki-taka and positional-play, which are about the technical/positional model itself: here the criterion is the purpose of possession (risk control, opponent denied the ball) and willingness to concede the ball or play deeper when needed (Xavi 2012: 'played 10-15 metres deeper'; Arteta 2020-21 loosening). Label is Cox-style analysts' and press framing, not a term the managers used. Window is long and discontinuous (2012-2019 gap) by design. No Spanish-language or Coaches' Voice / These Football Times page was readable: searches (b) marking and (e) PT/ES returned no usable primary page, so marking evidence is thin for Spain.
openQuestions: Ids: vicente-del-bosque (manager) and spain-2008-12 (team) exist in the catalog. Arteta has none: propose manager id 'mikel-arteta' and team id 'arsenal-2019-22' (not created).
Overlap with tiki-taka: Spain 2008-12 is also its core era. Keep this profile defined by risk control and conceding territory; confirm the distinction is acceptable.
Spain marking (zonal vs man): no source found; Arsenal's press is 'a mix of a zonal and man-oriented press' (Analytics FC, 2021/22 only).
Arteta end date of the window (2022-05-22) is approximate; spell is actually ongoing.
Del Bosque 'Possession without having depth' quote seen only in a search summary (attributed to Marca); no primary page.
Arteta quote about 'fast flowing, attacking football' (TBS) is a secondhand rewrite of an Arsenal.com interview; wording unconfirmed.

Contradiction on Arteta: Opta Analyst calls 2019/20 'overly rigid possession' while FourFourTwo (Mar 2021) says he abandoned Guardiola principles; Analytics FC says passing volume fell ~45 per match in 2021/22 with similar possession %. The 'control' label fits Spain more clearly than Arsenal after 2020.

statedView.quote: Possession without having depth doesn't have any point
statedView.source: Del Bosque to Marca, as relayed in a search summary only (page not mined)

statedView.quote: We play against very deep teams and we can’t change that. What we have to do is find a way to attack them, hurt them. But that has its good side too: they attack us less.
We have based our efficiency on good defensive order. We’ve been very solid.
We don't want to stagnate, we want to go forward but winning two trophies has been proof of our qualities. So we look to play in our style, people don't like it but it is our style
I want to do things my way but by convincing them that’s it’s the right way for everybody to live better.
My first task will be to get to know the players better and get them playing the kind of fast flowing, attacking football that Arsenal supporters around the world want to see.
statedView.source: TBS News 2019-12-20 (paraphrasing Arsenal.com interview; wording unconfirmed)
